title: Earnings week ahead: MSFT, AAPL, GOOG, AMZN, META, XOM, CVX, KO, V, SBUX, F, GM, and more
content:
[Magnifying Glass On Top Of Bar Chart Showing Decling Performance]
DNY59/iStock via Getty Images

As earnings season hits its peak, the week ahead stands out as one of the most consequential reporting stretches of the year.

Five members of the Magnificent Seven, Apple (AAPL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AAPL]), Microsoft (MSFT [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MSFT]), Amazon (AMZN [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AMZN]), Alphabet (GOOGL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GOOGL]), and Meta (META [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/META]), headline the calendar, placing a sharp spotlight on AI monetization, cloud demand, digital advertising, and consumer ecosystems.

Beyond big tech, the week spans a remarkably broad cross-section of the global economy.

Energy majors Exxon Mobil (XOM [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/XOM]), Chevron (CVX [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/CVX]), and ConocoPhillips (COP [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/COP]) will reflect commodity dynamics, while industrial bellwethers Caterpillar (CAT [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/CAT]), General Dynamics (GD [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GD]), and UPS offer a read on infrastructure, defense, and global logistics demand.

Consumer and payments giants like Coca-Cola (KO [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/KO]), Starbucks (SBUX [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/SBUX]), Chipotle (CMG [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/CMG]), Visa (V [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/V]), and Mastercard (MA [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MA]) will provide cues on spending resilience, and healthcare leaders Eli Lilly (LLY [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/LLY]), Merck (MRK [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MRK]), AbbVie (ABBV [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ABBV]), and Amgen (AMGN [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AMGN]) will highlight innovation pipelines and demand durability.

The calendar further extends into autos, telecom, fintech, and emerging tech, with Ford (F [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/F]), GM, T-Mobile (TMUS [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/TMUS]), Verizon (VZ [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/VZ]), Robinhood (HOOD [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/HOOD]), Roku (ROKU [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ROKU]), and Enphase Energy (ENPH [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ENPH]) adding depth across connectivity, retail investing, and clean energy.

Rounding out the week are names spanning digital platforms, materials, and semiconductors, including QUALCOMM (QCOM [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/QCOM]), Spotify (SPOT [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/SPOT]), Booking Holdings (BKNG [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/BKNG]), First Solar (FSLR [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/FSLR]), and Vale (VALE [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/VALE]).

With leadership stocks and cyclical sectors reporting side by side, this week's earnings will deliver one of the most comprehensive snapshots yet of global growth, corporate spending, and market direction, and a critical test of whether elevated expectations around AI, consumption, and macro resilience can hold.

Below is a rundown of major quarterly updates anticipated in the week of April 20 to April 24:

MONDAY, APRIL 27

VERIZON COMMUNICATIONS (VZ [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/VZ])

Verizon Communications (VZ [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/VZ]) is set to report Q1 results before Monday’s open, with analysts expecting modest Y/Y growth in both revenue and earnings.

Wall Street maintains a Buy rating, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant system remains more cautious at Hold [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/VZ/ratings/quant-ratings#source=firstLevelUrl%3Asymbol%7CbiSectionAsset%3ARatingSummary%7CbiName%3AQuant_rating], citing limited growth visibility.

SA VIEWS REMAIN MIXED:

Kenio Fontes recently downgraded the stock to Hold [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4891357-verizon-why-shareholders-should-fear-the-amazon-flywheel-downgrade], pointing to modest near-term momentum (2–3% revenue growth and 4–5% EPS guidance for 2026) amid intense competition from T-Mobile US and AT&T.

On the bullish side, The Alpha Analyst reiterates a Strong Buy [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4891143-verizon-stock-strong-buy-resilient-cash-flow-stable-valuation], viewing VZ as an income-focused play supported by resilient cash flows, ~9x forward earnings valuation, and robust capital return plans. Management’s focus on ~$5B in cost savings, disciplined capex, and steady free cash flow growth underpins dividend sustainability and buybacks.

In contrast, SA Investing Group Leader Stone Fox Capital maintains a Sell [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4891802-verizon-path-back-down-to-40], citing structural growth challenges, high leverage, and limited exposure to next-generation growth areas. Despite its ~6% yield, concerns around flat wireless growth and reliance on legacy assets could pressure long-term valuation.

 	* Consensus EPS Estimates: $1.21
 	* Consensus Revenue Estimates: $34.86B
 	* Earnings Insight: The company has exceeded EPS expectations in all the past 8 quarters and revenue estimates 50% of the time in that span.

TUESDAY, APRIL 28

COCA-COLA (KO [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/KO])

The Coca-Cola Company (KO [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/KO]) is set to report Q1 results before Tuesday’s open, with analysts expecting over 9% Y/Y growth in both revenue and earnings.

The company recently announced a $1B investment [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4571064-coca-cola-unveils-1b-south-africa-investment-plan-through-2030] in South Africa through 2030, alongside local bottling partners, aimed at expanding production, strengthening distribution, and driving product innovation, highlighting its asset-light, franchise-driven model.

Wall Street maintains a Buy rating, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant system is more cautious at Hold [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/KO/ratings/quant-ratings#source=firstLevelUrl%3Asymbol%7CbiSectionAsset%3ARatingSummary%7CbiName%3AQuant_rating], citing valuation concerns.

SA author YR Research reiterates a Buy [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4890277-coca-cola-the-retirement-dream], emphasizing Coca-Cola’s defensive appeal, consistent mid-single-digit organic growth, and strong dividend profile, with expected annual returns of 8–10%.

In contrast, SA Investing Group Leader Dhierin Bechai downgraded the stock to Hold [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4890598-coca-cola-buy-for-the-dividend-hold-for-the-upside-downgrade], noting limited upside after recent outperformance, with a price target implying modest gains despite stable cash flows and resilient fundamentals.

WEDNESDAY, APRIL 29

MICROSOFT CORPORATION (MSFT [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MSFT]), AMAZON.COM (AMZN [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AMZN]), META PLATFORMS (META [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/META]), AND ALPHABET (GOOG [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GOOG])

Wednesday shapes up as a pivotal moment for Big Tech, with four “Magnificent 7” names. Microsoft (MSFT [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MSFT]), Meta Platforms (META [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/META]), Amazon (AMZN [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AMZN]), and Alphabet (GOOGL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GOOGL]) are all set to report after the market closes, placing the spotlight firmly on AI, cloud, and digital advertising trends.

Heading into earnings, the narrative remains centered [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4576930-the-earnings-tightrope-will-mag-7-bulls-pivot-to-bottom-fishing] on AI-driven growth versus margin pressure. Microsoft’s Azure momentum is key, though rising CapEx continues to divide opinion. Meta is viewed constructively on pullbacks despite mixed reception to recent AI developments, while Alphabet’s steady growth is tempered by heavy investments in AI and adjacent ventures. Amazon, meanwhile, is doubling down on AI and infrastructure through its massive AWS investments, with markets closely watching returns on capital.

Wall Street maintains a Strong Buy across all four names, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant system takes a more measured stance with Hold ratings, reflecting valuation concerns.

However, SA author Gary Alexander rates Amazon a Sell [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4893417-amazon-sell-on-anthropic-deal-spike-valuation-doesnt-add-up], arguing its ~$2.7T valuation is difficult to justify despite recent momentum driven by AWS and AI partnerships.

Similarly, Dmytro Lebid sees Microsoft as a Sell [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4891641-microsoft-don-t-buy-the-dip-a-30-percent-correction-is-still-ahead], citing rising capital intensity, margin pressure, and potential multiple compression as the business shifts toward infrastructure-heavy AI investments.

THURSDAY, APRIL 30

APPLE (AAPL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AAPL])

California-based Apple (AAPL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AAPL]), another core member of the “Magnificent Seven,” is set to report FQ2 results after Thursday’s close, with analysts expecting ~18% Y/Y EPS growth on ~15% revenue expansion.

Recent developments have kept the spotlight on the iPhone maker. A major leadership transition is underway, with Tim Cook set to move into an Executive Chairman role and John Ternus stepping in as CEO, signaling a stronger product and engineering focus.

Meanwhile, iPhone shipments in China rose 20% in Q1, supported by the latest iPhone cycle, pricing actions, and government incentives.

Wall Street remains bullish, with Morgan Stanley viewing the upcoming print as a potential “clearing event,” driven by solid momentum across iPhone, Mac, and Services.

However, Seeking Alpha’s Quant Rating stays at Hold [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AAPL/ratings/quant-ratings#source=firstLevelUrl%3Asymbol%7CbiSectionAsset%3ARatingSummary%7CbiName%3AQuant_rating], citing valuation concerns.

SA views are notably divided.

Louis Gerard rates the stock a Sell [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4892801-apple-the-ceo-transition-is-a-multiple-compression-catalyst], flagging elevated multiples, AI execution risks, and potential margin pressure, while Given Mahlangu maintains a Strong Buy [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4892654-apple-stock-see-an-alchain-allen-theorem-at-play-upgrade-strong-buy], pointing to Apple’s pricing advantage and resilient demand dynamics.

Bill Maurer adopts a wait-and-watch [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4892392-apple-enters-new-leadership-era] stance, highlighting strong fundamentals but cautioning that premium valuation may limit near-term upside.

title: 5 Dividend Stocks Boost Payouts as Markets Reel Under Inflation Fears
content:
The U.S. economic landscape remains resilient. However, investors should remain cautious due to various domestic and geopolitical uncertainties. Inflation remains the primary concern as energy costs begin to bite. The Consumer Price Index jumped to 3.3% over the last 12 months in March, driven by a 21.2% spike in gasoline prices. While core inflation remains relatively stable at 2.6%, the wholesale side is seeing pressure, with the Producer Price Index hitting 4% year over year.

Looking ahead, the near-term outlook is heavily influenced by geopolitical developments, particularly the conflict in the Middle East, which has caused massive volatility in energy prices. However, hopes for a truce have brought some stability to oil prices. At the same time, ongoing conflicts involving Russia and Ukraine, as well as U.S.-China trade uncertainties, also pose downside risks. These factors can disrupt global supply chains, energy prices and global trade flows, which will eventually nudge inflation higher. The Federal Reserve has adopted a "wait-and-see" approach, holding interest rates between 3.5% and 3.75%. Elevated interest rates could negatively influence borrowing costs and corporate investment decisions.

As a result, cautious investors can diversify their portfolios and pick dividend-paying stocks. Some of the prominent names are: TANGER INC SKT, F.N.B. FNB, Johnson & Johnson JNJ, Constellation Brands STZ andKNOT Offshore Partners KNOP. Companies that pay out dividends consistently indicate a healthy business model. Stocks that have raised dividends recently exhibit a sound financial structure and can counter market upheavals. Moreover, stocks that tend to reward investors with a high dividend payout outperform non-dividend-paying entities in a highly volatile market.

TANGER INC

TANGER INC is a real estate investment trust, which acts as an operator of upscale open-air outlet centers, fully or partially owns and manages a portfolio of shopping centers principally in U.S. states and Canada. This Greensboro, NC-based company currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

On April 13, SKT declared that its shareholders would receive a dividend of 31 cents a share on May 15, 2026. SKT has a dividend yield of 3.2%.

Over the past five years, SKT has increased its dividend eight times, and its payout ratio presently sits at 50% of earnings. Check TANGER’s dividend history here.

title: Tanger (SKT) is a Top Dividend Stock Right Now: Should You Buy?
content:
All investors love getting big returns from their portfolio, whether it's through stocks, bonds, ETFs, or other types of securities. However, when you're an income investor, your primary focus is generating consistent cash flow from each of your liquid investments.

Cash flow can come from bond interest, interest from other types of investments, and, of course, dividends. A dividend is that coveted distribution of a company's earnings paid out to shareholders, and investors often view it by its dividend yield, a metric that measures the dividend as a percent of the current stock price. Many academic studies show that dividends account for significant portions of long-term returns, with dividend contributions exceeding one-third of total returns in many cases.

Headquartered in Greensboro, Tanger (SKT) is a Finance stock that has seen a price change of 9.86% so far this year. The factory outlet mall operator is currently shelling out a dividend of $0.29 per share, with a dividend yield of 3.19%. This compares to the REIT and Equity Trust - Retail industry's yield of 4.02% and the S&P 500's yield of 1.39%.

Looking at dividend growth, the company's current annualized dividend of $1.17 is up 1.5% from last year. Over the last 5 years, Tanger has increased its dividend 4 times on a year-over-year basis for an average annual increase of 14.37%. Looking ahead, future dividend growth will be dependent on earnings growth and payout ratio, which is the proportion of a company's annual earnings per share that it pays out as a dividend. Tanger's current payout ratio is 50%, meaning it paid out 50% of its trailing 12-month EPS as dividend.

SKT is expecting earnings to expand this fiscal year as well. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 is $2.46 per share, with earnings expected to increase 5.58% from the year ago period.

From greatly improving stock investing profits and reducing overall portfolio risk to providing tax advantages, investors like dividends for a variety of different reasons. However, not all companies offer a quarterly payout.

title: 3 Top-Ranked Dividend Stocks: A Smarter Way to Boost Your Retirement Income
content:
Believe it or not, seniors fear running out of cash more than they fear dying.

Also, retirees who have constructed a nest egg have valid justifications to be concerned, since the traditional ways to plan for retirement may mean income can no longer cover expenses. Some retirees are now tapping their principal to make a decent living, pressed for time between decreasing investment balances and longer life expectancies.

The tried - and - true retirement investing approach of yesterday doesn't work today.

Years ago, investors at or close to retirement could put money into fixed-income assets and depend on appealing yields to generate consistent, solid pay streams to fund a comfortable retirement. 10-year Treasury bond rates in the late 1990s floated around 6.50%, but unfortunately, those days of being able to exclusively rely on Treasury yields to fund retirement income are over.

The impact of this rate decline is sizable: over 20 years, the difference in yield for a $1 million investment in 10-year Treasuries is more than $1 million.

And lower bond yields aren't the only potential problem seniors are facing. Today's retirees aren't feeling as secure as they once did about Social Security, either. Benefit checks will still be coming for the foreseeable future, but based on current estimates, Social Security funds will run out of money in 2035.

So what can retirees do? You could dramatically reduce your expenses, and go out on a limb hoping your Social Security benefits don't diminish. On the other hand, you could opt for an alternative investment that gives a steady, higher-rate income stream to supplant lessening bond yields.

Invest in Dividend Stocks

Dividend-paying stocks from low-risk, high-quality companies are a smart way to generate steady and reliable attractive income streams to replace low risk, low yielding Treasury and bond options.

Look for stocks that have paid steady, increasing dividends for years (or decades), and have not cut their dividends even during recessions.

A rule of thumb for finding solid income-producing stocks is to seek those that average 3% dividend yield, and positive yearly dividend growth. These stocks can help combat inflation by boosting dividends over time.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks retirees should consider for their nest egg portfolio.

Phillips Edison & Company, Inc. (PECO) is currently shelling out a dividend of $0.11 per share, with a dividend yield of 3.38%. This compares to the REIT and Equity Trust - Retail industry's yield of 3.9% and the S&P 500's yield of 1.39%. The company's annualized dividend growth in the past year was 5.13%. The PNC Financial Services Group, Inc (PNC) is paying out a dividend of $1.70 per share at the moment, with a dividend yield of 3.07% compared to the Financial - Investment Bank industry's yield of 0.44% and the S&P 500's yield. The annualized dividend growth of the company was 3.23% over the past year. Check The PNC Financial Services Group, Inc dividend history here>>>

Currently paying a dividend of $0.31 per share, Tanger (SKT) has a dividend yield of 3.19%. This is compared to the REIT and Equity Trust - Retail industry's yield of 3.9% and the S&P 500's current yield. Annualized dividend growth for the company in the past year was 6.36%. Check Tanger dividend history here>>>

But aren't stocks generally more risky than bonds?

Overall, that is true. But stocks are a broad class, and you can reduce the risks significantly by selecting high-quality dividend stocks that can generate regular, predictable income and can also decrease the volatility of your portfolio compared to the overall stock market.

Combating the impact of inflation is one advantage of owning these dividend-paying stocks. Here's why: many of these stable, high-quality companies increase their dividends over time, which translates to rising dividend income that offsets the effects of inflation.

Thinking about dividend-focused mutual funds or ETFs? Watch out for fees.

If you're thinking, "I want to invest in a dividend-focused ETF or mutual fund," make sure to do your homework. It's important to know that some mutual funds and specialized ETFs charge high fees, which may diminish your dividend gains or income and thwart the overall objective of this investment strategy. If you do want to invest in fund, research well to identify the best-quality dividend funds with the least charges.

Bottom Line

Pursuing a dividend investing strategy can help protect your retirement portfolio. Whether you choose to invest in stocks or through low-fee mutual funds or ETFs, this approach can potentially help you achieve a more secure and enjoyable retirement.

title: Tanger Increases Dividend by 7%
content:
Declares Quarterly Dividend of 31.25 Cents per Share

GREENSBORO, N.C., April 13, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Tanger® (NYSE: SKT), a leading owner and operator of outlet and other open-air retail shopping destinations, announced today that its Board of Directors approved a 6.8% increase in the dividend on its common shares from $1.17 to $1.25 per share on an annualized basis. Simultaneously, the Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.3125 per share, payable on May 15, 2026 to common shareholders of record on April 30, 2026.

"Our dividend increase reflects the strength of Tanger’s operating platform, cash flow growth, and the discipline of our capital allocation strategy," said Stephen Yalof, President and Chief Executive Officer. "Our well-positioned balance sheet and low dividend payout ratio provide Tanger with the liquidity and flexibility to continue to invest in our long-term growth initiatives and create long-term value for our stakeholders through asset appreciation and dividend growth."

About Tanger®

Tanger Inc. (NYSE: SKT) is a leading owner and operator of outlet and other open-air retail shopping destinations, with 45 years of expertise in the retail and outlet shopping industries. Tanger's portfolio of 38 outlet centers and three open-air lifestyle centers includes more than 16 million square feet well positioned across tourist destinations and vibrant markets in 22 U.S. states and Canada. A publicly traded REIT since 1993, Tanger continues to innovate the retail experience for its shoppers with over 3,000 stores operated by more than 800 different brand name companies.
